definitions.explanation: A person employed to do household work or attend to the needs of a master or household. In modern usage, primarily appears in historical, literary, or fantasy contexts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{屋敷|やしき}→屋敷：12395_yashiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{何人|なんにん}→何人：17593_nannin⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{召使|めしつか}いがいた。
examples.english: There were many servants in the mansion.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{貴族|きぞく}→貴族：17414_kizoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大勢|おおぜい}→大勢：02850_oozei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{召使|めしつか}い⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{囲|かこ}まれて→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧⟦{暮|く}らしていた→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧。
examples.english: Nobles of old lived surrounded by many servants.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {召使|めしつか}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{雇|やと}う→雇う：02320_yatou⟧ (hire a servant)
- {召使|めしつか}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{呼|よ}ぶ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧ (call a servant)
- ⟦{忠実|ちゅうじつ}→忠実：12570_chuujitsu⟧な{召使|めしつか}い (a loyal servant)

Derived from {召|め}し{使|つか}う (to employ, to summon and use). In contemporary Japanese, this word is mostly found in historical dramas, period novels, fairy tales, and fantasy settings. For modern domestic workers, ⟦{家事|かじ}→家事：12313_kaji⟧⟦ヘルパー→ヘルパー：11284_herupaa⟧ or ⟦{家政婦|かせいふ}→家政婦：12496_kaseifu⟧ are used instead.
